STORIES · IN ISPUTNIK.HOME

The family’s stories, written down.
With the photos right where they belong.

A story is a page you write together: your words, with photos, videos, maps, people from the tree, and grandma’s voice telling the ending. It points at what’s already in the house — it never copies it.

Get iSputnik ↗See what it does ↓
  • No cloud needed
  • No ads
  • No hidden costs
  • No tracking

WHAT IT DOES

Write it once. Keep it for good.

Write

Start from a shape, then make it yours.

  • A story, a memory, a travel blog, a review or a recipe
  • Travel blogs laid out day by day from the trip’s dates
  • Chapters, each with its own cover, date and place
  • Photos, albums, slideshows, maps, books and people as blocks
  • A draft only you see, until you publish it

Read and listen

A story reads like a small website of its own.

  • A reading view with no app around it
  • A map of the journey, one pin per chapter
  • Every chapter in view beside the page
  • Narration recorded in the editor, or an old recording uploaded
  • Day before and day after, at the foot of each chapter

Recipes and reviews

Two kinds of story every family keeps anyway.

  • Recipes start with Ingredients, Method and Notes
  • Paste a link to a recipe page and it’s written for you
  • Serves and total time on the recipe’s front page
  • A review with stars, from any book’s page
  • A review of the audiobook shows on the ebook too

Share and shelve

Hand a story on, or keep it among the people it belongs to.

  • Collections like Family Story or Trips, laid out year by year
  • Private collections, with View, Contribute and Manage
  • Send a story to someone’s inbox
  • Guest links for relatives without an account
  • A deleted story waits in the recycle bin, whole

PRIVATE HERE, SPECIFICALLY

A story never shows more than it should.

The general promises hold everywhere. These are the ones that matter most for stories.

Nobody sees what they couldn’t already

Every photo, album and book in a story is checked against the reader’s own access. Anything out of their reach shows as a polite placeholder, not a leak.

Guest links you stay in charge of

A guest sees the story as it is now, and only what the story shows — whole albums only if you say so. Delete the story and its links stop answering.

Nothing is copied

A story points at what’s already in the house. Delete it, and every photo, book and recording it pointed at stays exactly where it was.

A recipe page read once

Starting a recipe from a link reads that page’s text and keeps nothing but what lands in your story. An administrator can switch it off altogether.

QUESTIONS

About stories.

More in the Stories guide and Exposing to the internet.

Does a story copy my photos?

No. The photo in a story is the photo in your gallery: rotate it or tag someone in it, and the story shows the change.

Can relatives without an account read it?

Yes. Send → Share link makes a guest link that opens in any browser, no account needed.

Can I record grandma telling it?

Yes. Add → Narration records right in the editor, up to fifteen minutes a take — or upload a recording you already have.

What happens if I delete a story?

It goes to the recycle bin, whole — chapters, stars, guest links and all — and can be restored for 30 days, unless your administrator set a different time.
